reason: The rover is making one last invitation, so the welcome banner looks like a useful surface for it.
expectation: The rover will draw a welcome message or picture on the banner.

effect: The banner is decorated and ready to welcome the guests.
reaction: Kit's whale in a cardboard hat is a nice detail.
reason: The finished banner belongs at the fair, so I’ll try attaching it there.
expectation: The welcome banner will be displayed at the fair.

effect: The banner is hung clear of the tether lines, and the controls are ready.
reaction: Keeping the banner clear of the lines makes practical sense.
reason: The attractions need their switch to run for the fair; I’ll try that before lifting the whale.
expectation: The dragon and star theatre will start operating.

effect: The dragon and star theatre are running; the remaining step is to lift the whale.
reaction: Seeing both attractions work together makes the flight feel close.
reason: The lift-control key should operate the prepared flying fair.
expectation: The whale will rise under control while the attractions run.

effect: The lift brought the tethered whale into the air, opening the flying fair and completing the goal.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the dragon and stars working aboard the flying whale, with Kit invited to take a turn.

mostWorthwhile.text: Switching on the attractions was worthwhile because it brought the dragon and star theatre together before the flight.

leastWorthwhile.text: Hanging the finished banner was a straightforward placement, with less to figure out than the other moments.

surprise.text: The banner went across the grounded cradle rather than onto the whale itself, keeping it clear of the tether lines.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary; the banner and two controls each had a clear role.

continue.text: I would continue for another construction challenge if it offered a new mechanism to figure out; this finale was satisfying, though its actions were mostly predictable.
